public_rationale: Microsoft reports paid Copilot adoption and a contribution to revenue-per-user growth. Alphabet reports AI-associated Search gains. These disclosures challenge the claim's breadth. However, the available measures do not isolate realized AI revenue from non-investee customers. Under the required metric-matching rule, they remain context rather than decisive revenue evidence.
limitations: The result is sensitive to whether AI-assisted existing products count as AI revenue.
Lack of a separate revenue disclosure does not establish lack of revenue.
No list-price multiplication of paid seats was used.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hyperscalers have no meaningful AI revenue beyond their investee AI labs.

statement.excerpt: Hyperscalers do not have meaningful AI revenues of any kind outside of their own pseudo-startup investments

from_speaker: do not have meaningful AI revenues of any kind
outside of their own pseudo-startup investments
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that hyperscalers lack a substantial commercial AI revenue business serving customers other than their investee labs.
Meaningful means commercially substantial, not necessarily profitable or sufficient to recover capital expenditure.
The exclusion concerns investee labs as paying customers. Selling an AI product to an unrelated enterprise is not automatically excluded merely because the product uses a lab's model.
I use January–March 2026, the latest common reportable calendar quarter before the post.
The surrounding argument relies on company-disclosed AI revenue, so the contract uses company_reported accounting basis.
criteria.support_condition: Customer-level realized AI revenue disclosures show that revenue outside investee labs was negligible across the relevant hyperscalers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one hyperscaler demonstrates commercially substantial realized AI revenue from customers outside its investee labs during the target period.

evidence.locator: Amy Hood prepared remarks, Productivity and Business Processes
evidence.explanation: The same discussion reports more than 20 million paid Copilot seats and attributes revenue-per-user growth partly to Copilot. This materially challenges the broad assertion, but neither seat counts nor blended revenue-per-user growth measures standalone realized AI revenue excluding investees.

Alphabet identifies commercial benefits associated with AI outside direct lab infrastructure purchases. Total Search revenue growth does not isolate AI revenue or establish its customer composition, so this remains countervailing context.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Realized quarterly revenue for a substantial AI product or customer segment, with investee-lab purchases excluded and the recognition basis stated.
